text.p: Burma's military government said on Saturday it has sentenced 20 people to seven years in prison each for their involvement in street demonstrations in December.
The 20 included six members of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party, led by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.

"These 20 persons were inciting and agitating students and non-students during December 1996 student demonstrations and it is learnt that none of them are students," said a statement by Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) obtained by Reuters. It gave no further details.
A spokesman for Suu Kyi told Reuters she had no comment on the sentencing because she was still trying to find out more details.
"We heard about that, but we are trying to confirm if it's true," the spokesman said by telephone.
The 20 people were arrested after demonstrations in December, when thousands of students took to the street in a week of protests against the military government.
It was the largest act of defiance against the government since 1988 national demonstrations which were eventually quashed by the SLORC in a bloody crackdown that left thousands dead or in jail.
The SLORC has accused Suu Kyi's party of politicising the demonstrations. Suu Kyi has denied the allegation, but said she and her party support the students demand for justice.
In a news conference earlier this month Suu Kyi lashed out at the SLORC for its continued repression of the democracy movement, and for confining her to her house.
The government has arrested and released more than 1,000 NLD members since last May in a series of crackdowns on the movement. At least 100 are still being held as political prisoners, Suu Kyi said.
"They seem to be very happy arresting people. They seem to enjoy arresting people, it's going on all the time," Suu Kyi told the January 4 news conference.
Suu Kyi has been under virtual house arrest since the December unrest.
The government says it is for her own protection but Suu Kyi, who was released from six years of official house arrest in July 1995, says the confinement does help her at all.
The NLD won a landslide victory in a 1990 election, but the SLORC refused to recognise the results of the vote.
